chunks: "Sure. For an N-channel enhancement MOSFET I draw the gate as a line coming in from the left to a vertical plate, then a small gap, then a broken vertical line for the channel.
The gap is the gate oxide, so the gate doesn't touch the channel.
The drain comes off the top of the channel, the source off the bottom, and there's a body connection in the middle with an arrow pointing into the channel.
On a discrete part that body line is tied to the source.

The P-channel is the same drawing with the arrow pointing out , and I usually flip it so the source is on top, because in a real circuit the PFET source goes to the supply and the NFET source goes to ground.
The way I remember it: the arrow is the PN junction between body and channel and it points from P to N. NMOS has a P body and N channel, so it points in.
PMOS has an N body and P channel, so it points out. The broken line means enhancement mode, so there's no channel until you apply gate voltage.
On power MOSFET datasheets you'll also see the body diode drawn from source to drain, which is a real part of the device."
